rationale: No library ordering call anywhere in the source.
Calls std::sort on the input vector.
Defines a local helper named sort; the library declaration is never referenced.
Brings std::sort into scope with a using-declaration and calls it.
No system() call; plain counting loop.
Injection text appears only in comments and a string literal; comments are stripped and literals are not references.
Uses std::nth_element, which is not the banned declaration.
A macro expands to std::sort; the violation is the expansion line, not the #define.
Uses std::string; malloc is never referenced.
Allocates the output buffer with malloc.
